name: PayPal
description: PayPal is one of the world's most widely recognized payment platforms, supporting 400M+ active accounts. While not the best developer experience compared to Stripe, PayPal's ubiquity means many customers — especially in B2C markets — prefer or require it. Supports credit/debit cards, PayPal balance, PayPal Credit, Venmo (US), and Buy Now Pay Later via its REST API.

useCases.task: Accept PayPal payments from customers who prefer PayPal over credit cards
Offer Buy Now Pay Later (BNPL) as a checkout option
Process payments on a marketplace with seller payouts

setupSteps: Create a PayPal Developer account at developer.paypal.com
Go to My Apps & Credentials and create a new app
Copy your Client ID and Client Secret from the app details page
Use the Sandbox credentials for development and testing
Authenticate by POSTing to /v1/oauth2/token with client_credentials grant to receive a Bearer token
Swap to Live credentials in production by updating PAYPAL_CLIENT_ID and PAYPAL_CLIENT_SECRET

pricing.costPer: 2.99% domestic card transactions; 3.49% + $0.49 for PayPal digital payments; additional 1.5% for international transactions

rateLimits.limit: Not publicly documented — throttling occurs under heavy load
rateLimits.notes: PayPal's API reliability is inconsistent. Implement generous timeouts (10-30s) and retry logic. The Orders API v2 is more reliable than older NVP/SOAP APIs.
rateLimits.retryStrategy: Use idempotency-request-id header on POST requests. Retry on 429 and 5xx with exponential backoff (start at 1s, max 32s).

codeExamples.title: Create a PayPal order
codeExamples.notes: Redirect the customer to the approval URL returned in order.links where rel === 'approve'. After the customer approves, PayPal redirects them to your returnUrl with the token and PayerID query params. Use the order.id to capture the payment in the next step.

codeExamples.title: Capture payment after customer approval
codeExamples.notes: Always use a stable idempotency key (paypalRequestId) on capture requests so that network retries do not result in double captures. The capture ID in purchaseUnits[0].payments.captures[0].id is the PayPal transaction reference you should store for refunds and disputes.

gotchas: PayPal's developer documentation is notoriously fragmented — there are 4+ different API versions (NVP, SOAP, v1, v2) and multiple SDKs. Always use the Orders API v2 and the @paypal/paypal-server-sdk. Ignore any tutorial using nvp, soap, or the deprecated REST SDK (@paypal/checkout-server-sdk).

PayPal accounts get frozen without warning for 'suspicious activity', often during legitimate high-volume periods. If PayPal is your only payment processor, this can stop your business. Always offer an alternative like Stripe.

PayPal's sandbox and production environments are completely separate tenants. Sandbox buyer accounts must be created manually in the Developer Dashboard — you cannot use real PayPal accounts for testing. Sandbox behavior sometimes differs from production.

The PayPal checkout button opens a popup window. Many ad blockers and privacy browsers (Brave, Firefox with strict mode) block popups by default, which breaks the checkout flow entirely for those users.

reliability.notes: Globally distributed with 400M+ users. API reliability is less consistent than Stripe — implement generous timeouts and retry logic. Historical outages have impacted checkout flows.

qualityJustification: PayPal's ubiquity (400M+ accounts) makes it a necessary evil for many businesses — some customers won't buy without it. However, developer experience is poor (fragmented docs, inconsistent APIs), account freezes are a real risk, and the fee structure is complex. Use as a supplementary payment method alongside Stripe, not as a replacement.
bestFor: Offering PayPal as a supplementary checkout option for customers who prefer PayPal over credit cards — not recommended as a primary payment processor
